claims.text: The proposed modular LLM pipeline semantically extracts features from textual patient admission records.
Qwen-14B-Chat achieved an accuracy of 95.52% and a precision of 92.93% in clinical feature extraction.
Baichuan2-13B-Chat achieved an accuracy of 95.86% and a precision of 90.08% in clinical feature extraction.
An INT4-quantified version of Qwen-14B-Chat achieved 97.28% accuracy and a 0% null ratio on consumer-grade hardware.

evidence.description: The pipeline processes a systematic succession of concept extraction, aggregation, question generation, corpus extraction, and question-and-answer scale extraction.
Evaluation on 25,709 pregnancy cases yielded accuracy and precision results of 95.52% and 92.93% for Qwen-14B-Chat.
Evaluation on 25,709 pregnancy cases yielded accuracy and precision results of 95.86% and 90.08% for Baichuan2-13B-Chat.
An INT4-quantified version of QWEN evaluated on a consumer-grade GPU delivered 97.28% accuracy and a 0% null ratio.

methodologies.name: Modular LLM Extraction Pipeline
methodologies.description: A pipeline processing concept extraction, aggregation, question generation, corpus extraction, and Q&A scale extraction to extract features from clinical records.
datasets: 25,709 pregnancy cases from the People's Hospital of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China

limitations.text: Large language models present security and feature hallucination issues in clinical applications.
